route: published per-item CFA/EFA loadings (Fig 1, Fig 3) + keying polarity + alpha-if-deleted, with 8! permutation uniqueness
evidence: Route 1 variant (per-item published factor loadings) + route 6 (keying polarity) + alpha, all on the live table (605 respondents) vs the paper's non-clinical sample (602); re-run with verify_ruiz_parra_2023_rfq8.R -> VERDICT: PASS. (A) Fig 1 one-factor WLSMV CFA, item 7 reversed, 3~~4: published loadings items 1-8 = .25/.68/.56/.52/.46/.84/.36/.53, observed .26/.70/.59/.54/.51/.88/.37/.58 (max |diff| .05); error covariance 3~~4 published .59, observed .63. (B) Fig 3 two-factor Promax EFA (ML on Pearson): published F1 item2 .74, item5 .38, item6 .77, item7 .44, item8 .44 / F2 item3 .81, item4 .82, item1 <.30 on both; observed F1 .74/.37/.76/.45/.42, F2 .85/.87, item1 .24/.02, all greyed cells <.30 (max salient |diff| .047). (C) Table 2 alpha .763 vs observed .767; text says removing item 1 raises alpha to .779, observed item 1 alpha-if-dropped .780 and it is the largest of the 8 (but item 7's .770 also marginally exceeds full alpha .767 in the live data, unlike the paper's 'only item 1'). (D) Raw polarity: RFQ8_7 correlates negatively with all 7 other items (-.12 to -.30); every other item has exactly one negative correlation, the one with RFQ8_7 -- pins item 7 ('I always know what I feel'). UNIQUENESS: over all 40320 reassignments of observed item vectors to published slots, the claimed mapping is the unique minimum misfit (.0127). Single-transposition cost as a multiple of identity: 3<->4 1.3x, 5<->8 2.4x, 5<->7 4.0x, 2<->6 5.8x, 7<->8 6.7x, 1<->7 7.9x, all others 11x-156x. NOT ESTABLISHED: the order within the 3/4 pair. Items 3 ('say things without really knowing why') and 4 ('say things I later regret') are near-collinear (raw r=.71); the EFA does not separate them (.81/.82) and the CFA preference rests on a published loading gap of .04 (.56 vs .52), about one SE at this N, so the 3<->4 swap costs only 1.3x. Everything else is distinguished (5<->8 at 2.4x is the next-weakest). Hence PARTIAL, not VERIFIED. The Fig 2 two-factor CFA was tried as a tiebreaker and rejected: it is a Heywood solution (published 1.34) and refits unstably.
